summary: Bulk dashboard rename left alert bindings orphaned after retention compaction
description:
Issue summary:
Customer performed a bulk rename of ~120 dashboards through the console bulk-rename flow. After the retention compaction job ran later that night, ~18 alert rules that had been bound to the renamed dashboards lost their binding and now appear as orphaned alerts pointing to the old dashboard slugs. Some orphaned alerts are still resolvable via the dashboard UI but their tracehook links no longer resolve and scheduled snapshot jobs for those dashboards fail with 404s.

Impact:
- Customer (NimbleAI) reported missing alert context in Slack notifications and failing scheduled snapshots for 18 dashboards.
- Affects monitoring and runbook automation that depends on tracehook links embedded in alerts.
- Business impact: delayed on-call response, snapshot reports not generated for scheduled reporting.

Environment:
- prod - us-east
- Console version: 2.14.1 (release tag: release/2026-03)
- Retention compaction job: compact-v4, nightly run 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Create dashboard with route slug `team-quickstart-<id>` and attach alert rule with tracehook link to `tracehook://runbook/abc123` and scheduled snapshot enabled.
2) Use Console bulk-rename feature to rename a set of dashboards (applies slug rewrite + metadata update).
3) Wait for nightly retention compaction / eviction job to run (compact-v4).
4) Observe alert rules referencing old slug show as orphaned in Alerts listing and scheduled snapshots for renamed dashboards fail with 404 referencing old slug.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Alert index query around 2026-03-10T02:35:12Z returned rules where `dashboard_slug` = `team-quickstart-123` but `dashboard.exists` = false.
- Snapshot scheduler error (scheduler-12) 2026-03-10T03:01:07Z: `Snapshot failed: dashboard lookup 404 for slug=team-quickstart-123`
- Retention compaction job logs: compact-v4: processed folder `dashboards/2026/03/10`, rewrite-map applied, then eviction took place.
- Console UI: Alerts list shows `-- orphaned --` for 18 rules, clicking tracehook link returns 404 page.

Additional notes:
- Customer provided CSV of renamed dashboards and a sample orphaned alert IDs: [A-3382, A-3383, A-3399, A-3401].
- Customer initially discovered when their nightly report emails failed and they received Slack alert messages with broken links.
- No model-serving impact; scope confined to Console metadata and alerting integrations.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial intake from NimbleAI. Collected CSV list of original and new slugs, example alert IDs, and sample snapshot failure logs. Ticket created and triaged.

2026-03-10 14:45 - Marco Hernandez (Console Eng): Confirmed replication on staging by running bulk-rename flow and triggering compact-v4. Observed orphaned bindings. Escalating to retention team. Posting results to #support and #infra-retention.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Leah O'Connor (Retention): Hypothesis: compaction eviction step deletes metadata rows before rename mapping is applied to alert bindings in the alerting index. Added INT-4021 for internal follow-up and suggested short-term reconciliation script.

2026-03-12 17:05 - Marco Hernandez (Console Eng): Reconciliation script prepared to remap alert.dashboard_slug using bulk-rename manifest. Requested approval to run against customer org (dry-run first).
investigation_notes: Retention compaction run order: 1) rewrite mappings from rename manifest, 2) eviction of abandoned objects, 3) index compaction. In compact-v4 we observed step 2 and 3 executing before step 1 for dashboards created in the same maintenance window.

Alerting index stores a denormalized `dashboard_slug` value; there is no foreign-key enforcement. When rewrite runs after eviction, alerting rows reference non-existent slugs resulting in orphaned alerts.

Repro on staging using 130 dashboards: bulk rename + compact-v4 => 12 orphaned alerts. Dry-run reconciliation would locate candidate alerts where `dashboard.exists=false` and a rename mapping exists, then patch alert row to new slug.

Retention team root cause candidate: race condition in compaction orchestration where rename manifest application to dependent indexes is scheduled on a best-effort background queue which can lag under high metadata churn.

Risk assessment: reconciliation script is low-risk if run in dry-run then patch mode. Persistent fix requires changing compaction orchestrator to apply rename/rewrite to all dependent indices before eviction or to add a pre-eviction lock for dashboards with active alert bindings.
resolution:
Workaround: Ran reconciliation script 2026-03-13 (after customer approval) in patch mode for NimbleAI: remapped 18 alert.dashboard_slug entries using customer's bulk-rename manifest; verified scheduled snapshots succeed and tracehook links resolve.
Permanent fix: Retention team to update compact-v4 orchestration (PR linked) to enforce rewrite-before-evict ordering for dashboard metadata and add integration test for alert-binding preservation. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention/pull/89 merged to main and scheduled for release 2026-03-20.
Follow-ups: Add monitoring alert to detect >5 orphaned alerts generated within a single compaction run and run reconciliation weekly on a low-traffic window until release rolls out.
